# Canon — THE CONDITION REPORT

Hard facts. Every entry is a constraint the evaluator checks against. If the
prose contradicts canon, it is a bug. One fact per bullet, source in
parentheses.

---

## Geography & Access

- Corvelijn & Zonen trades from Kloosterstraat 118, Antwerp, a four-floor
  brick house of 1883 with a cellar. (world.md)
- Sebastiaan owns Kloosterstraat 118 personally and outright; it is not firm
  property and is not pledged to anyone. (world.md)
- The ground floor is the firm: front office, strongroom, and Sebastiaan's
  office, where the 1974 deed hangs framed on the wall. (world.md)
- The white room is the conservation studio on the third floor, built in
  2017, north light through filtered glass, held at 50% relative humidity
  and 19°C. (world.md)
- The white room's dehumidifier is audible everywhere above the second
  landing, and it cuts out when the third-floor landing door is held open.
  (world.md, ch_03)
- The hot tap on the third floor at Kloosterstraat has never worked.
  (world.md, ch_04)
- Keys to Kloosterstraat 118: Sebastiaan, Kasimir Ott, and Ineke Claes the
  cleaner. Lena holds a white-room key from 15 January. (world.md, ch_03)
- The house alarm code is 1109. Sebastiaan has never changed it and has told
  only Lena. (world.md, ch_06)
- The cellar at 118 has no light switch at the top of the stairs, and the
  sluice under Kloosterstraat is audible through the floor all year.
  (world.md, ch_31)
- The Deurne depot is on Ten Eekhovelei: a 1930s grain store, concrete
  floor, freight lift with a folding gate, roller door that closes in three
  stages. (world.md)
- The depot's only heating is a wall unit with a faulty thermostat that runs
  nine minutes and stops for fifty. (world.md, ch_25)
- The depot's camera system was specified in 2014 and never wired; the empty
  housings are still on the beams. (world.md, ch_08)
- Keys to the depot: Kasimir Ott, plus one spare in the firm's strongroom.
  (world.md)
- Lena's flat is on Lange Riddersstraat, second floor rear, one room and a
  kitchen, damp in the corner by the window. (world.md)
- Lena's building was bought on 4 March by a vehicle whose sole director is a
  notary's clerk in Ekeren, funded from the firm's operating account. She was
  not evicted. (world.md, ch_22)
- Studio 4B is the drying and pressing room at the Royal Academy of Fine
  Arts, Mutsaardstraat: twelve presses, drying racks, north windows, a
  kettle. (world.md, ch_01)
- Access to Studio 4B is by conservator's key only. There are nineteen keys.
  (world.md, ch_01)
- Corvelijn & Zonen has been barred from Academy premises since 2019 by a
  standing minute of the faculty board, arising from a dispute over a loaned
  Beke study. (world.md, ch_01, ch_11)
- Studio 4B is the only ground in Antwerp Sebastiaan cannot walk onto.
  (world.md, ch_27)
- The Commission for the Restitution of Cultural Property is on Rue de la
  Loi, Brussels; its registry closes at 16:00 and does not accept filings out
  of hours. (world.md)
- Antwerp to Brussels is 45 minutes by train, four trains an hour.
  (world.md)
- Antwerp to Rotterdam is 90 minutes by train. (world.md)
- Kloosterstraat to the Deurne depot is 20 minutes by van, 35 by tram and
  foot. (world.md)
- Armand Brassart lives in a first-floor flat in Berchem with his tools still
  on the wall and the bench cleared. (characters.md)
- Souad Ferhat's bindery is in Sint-Andries, Antwerp; her sister's bindery is
  in Rotterdam. (characters.md, ch_15)
- Emiel Vandewiele's cordage yard is in Deurne and smells of tar and new
  rope. (ch_08)

## Timeline

- The book spans nineteen weeks: Monday 8 January to Thursday 21 May.
  (outline.md)
- 8 January (ch_01): Lena is working the Van der Weyden fragment and receives
  the firm's offer of four months' condition work. (ch_01)
- 15 January (ch_03): Lena's first day in the white room; she is given a key.
  (ch_03)
- 18 January (ch_04): Sebastiaan files the forty-page Zurich condition report
  over Lena's forged signature; Bram Six obtains a same-day date-stamp.
  (ch_04)
- 22 January (ch_05): Lena receives the courtesy copy and travels to Brussels
  on the 08:41. (ch_05)
- 26 January (ch_07): Lena's first meeting with advocaat Griet Vervoort.
  (ch_07)
- 31 January (ch_09): Lena refuses to sign the Feininger report and leaves an
  unsigned true condition report on the white-room table. (ch_09)
- 2 February (ch_10): Sebastiaan instructs Kasimir to make Tomas Beke
  unavailable. (ch_10)
- 6 February (ch_11): Tomas Beke is arrested; his archive accreditation is
  suspended the same morning. (ch_11)
- 9 February (ch_12): Sebastiaan reads the 1974 deed properly for the first
  time in nine years. (ch_12)
- 12 February (ch_13, ch_14): Lena sets her three terms; the burn in the
  yard. (ch_13, ch_14)
- 20 February (ch_16): Hanne Vandewiele appears for the first time. (ch_16)
- 22 February (ch_17): Lena manufactures the 1953 Basel loan receipt
  overnight in Studio 4B and seeds it into the Zurich annex file. (ch_17)
- 26 February (ch_19): the negotiated scene; the word "Basel" is set.
  (ch_19)
- 28 February (ch_20): Lena discovers she burned a laser print. (ch_20)
- 4 March (ch_22): Sebastiaan lodges the 1997 summary on the preliminary
  docket; the Ekeren purchase of Lena's building completes. (ch_22)
- 11 March (ch_23): Lena meets Dries Neefs. (ch_23)
- 12 March, 06:00 (ch_23): *De Wacht* publishes. Clause 22 fires by 09:30.
  (ch_23)
- 14 March (ch_24): Kasimir proposes moving "the researcher"; Sebastiaan says
  nothing. (ch_24)
- 15 to 25 March (ch_25, ch_26): Lena is held at the Deurne depot. Eleven
  days. (ch_25)
- 18 March: Sebastiaan learns she is at the depot. He does nothing until 25
  March. (ch_24, ch_27)
- 25 March (ch_26): Sebastiaan comes to the depot at eleven in the morning
  and drives her home. (ch_26)
- 27 March (ch_27): the Academy suspends Lena pending inquiry and takes her
  4B key at the front desk. (ch_27)
- 31 March (ch_27): the Vier's quarterly reckoning. Second miss recorded;
  extension to 30 June at sixteen per cent; audit findings due 15 April.
  (ch_27)
- 4 April (ch_28): the hand clinic. Nine days after release. (ch_28)
- 12 April (ch_29): Sebastiaan names Lena as the forger of the 1953 receipt,
  in Emiel Vandewiele's kitchen. (ch_29)
- 14 April (ch_30): Lena leaves Antwerp on the 22:07 to Rotterdam. (ch_30)
- 18 April (ch_31): Sebastiaan opens the four boxes and then goes to Rue de
  la Loi unannounced. (ch_31)
- 24 April (ch_32): Lena writes out her account of 22 February in longhand
  and decides to file it. (ch_32)
- 2 May: the Academy fellowship board meets. The Van der Weyden treatment is
  unpublished. The fellowship is lost. (ch_34)
- **Tuesday 5 May (ch_33): Sebastiaan files the corrigendum and the clause 9
  resignation at the Rue de la Loi registry at 15:40.** The hold ends here.
  (ch_33)
- 5 May, evening: the referral against B-4471 is withdrawn; a fresh referral
  is opened against Sebastiaan. (ch_33)
- **Friday 8 May (ch_33, ch_34): Emiel Vandewiele dies of a cardiac event in
  his kitchen, aged 74 — three days after the corrigendum.** (ch_33)
- 8 May (ch_34): Vervoort telephones; Armand is told; the tuition fact is
  disclosed. (ch_34)
- 14 May (ch_35): the Commission strikes Sebastiaan from the register for
  five years; the claim book leaves the building under seal; the name comes
  off the door. (ch_35)
- 15 May (ch_36): Ruth Schindler-Wolff in Antwerp; Tomas Beke in the
  bookshop. (ch_36)
- 19 May (ch_37): the Zurich tribunal rules in the Faller matter, awarding
  €6.2 million to the Corvelijn escrow. (ch_37)
- 19 May (ch_38): Lena's 4B key is returned. (ch_38)
- 21 May (ch_38): the final chapter. (ch_38)
- Historical: October 1997 — Lucien Corvelijn forges a 1938 export stamp;
  Armand Brassart signs the report; Sebastiaan, 19, holds the lamp and cuts
  the paper. (characters.md)
- Historical: 1999 — Godelieve Brassart dies. (characters.md)
- Historical: 2009 — Armand does it a second time, on a Munch drawing. Lena
  sees. (characters.md)
- Historical: 2013 — Lucien Corvelijn pays Lena's third-year tuition.
  (characters.md, ch_34)
- Historical: 2016 — Lucien Corvelijn dies; the Vier buy his operating debt
  at 58 cents on the euro; Sebastiaan takes the chair. (world.md)
- Historical: 2018 — Sebastiaan and Meike divorce. (characters.md)
- Historical: 2019 — the Academy loan dispute bars the firm from the
  premises; Dries Neefs's first piece is killed pre-publication; the firm
  buys the Maurice Faller estate archive at auction. (world.md)

## Power & Leverage

- Corvelijn & Zonen takes a contingent commission of 22–40% of hammer value
  on recovered works, depending on how cold the trail was. It is lawful.
  (world.md)
- The claim book is a bound calfskin register of sixty live claims, updated
  by hand since 1951 and mirrored in a database. (world.md)
- The claim book is valued by the firm at €38–44 million in future
  commission. (world.md)
- The claim book is firm property and is pledged to the Deurne Vier.
  (world.md)
- The index — eleven filing drawers and a laptop of forty years' private
  research — is Sebastiaan's personal property under clause 14 of the 1974
  deed. (world.md, ch_12)
- The Deurne Vier are owed €4.1 million plus eleven per cent, secured by
  pledge over the claim book. (world.md)
- The Vier take a quarterly reckoning on the last day of each quarter. Three
  consecutive misses entitle them to appoint their own administrator.
  (world.md)
- As of 8 January, Sebastiaan has missed one reckoning. He misses a second on
  31 March. (ch_08, ch_27)
- Clause 22 of the pledge: any public allegation of professional misconduct
  triggers an immediate audit right. (ch_08)
- Clause 9 of the 1974 deed: a *bewindvoerder* may resign by transferring the
  claim book into the escrow of a competent public authority, whereupon the
  personal liability transfers with it. (ch_12)
- The 1974 deed binds the stewardship to the eldest surviving Corvelijn while
  any pledge is outstanding. Sebastiaan cannot sell, wind up, retire, or
  refuse the office. (world.md)
- Emiel Vandewiele's undisclosed second schedule to the pledge, written in
  2016, passes the Vier's controlling vote to his estate on his death rather
  than to the remaining three. (characters.md, ch_37)
- Bram Six, a Commission clerk, has taken cash from the firm since 2013 for
  advance sight of filings and occasional delayed date-stamps. (world.md)
- Bram Six is never exposed in this book. (outline.md)
- Rachida Bekkali can strike an intermediary from the register of recognised
  representatives on her own authority. (world.md)
- A struck intermediary cannot appear, cannot file, and cannot take a
  contingent commission in Belgium. Provenance research for museums is not
  covered by the bar. (world.md, ch_37)
- Rachida does not strike the firm on suspicion because doing so suspends
  sixty live claims. (world.md)
- Armand Brassart signed the 1997 Kirchner report for 400,000 Belgian francs.
  (world.md)
- Between 1997 and 2009 Armand authenticated the paper evidence in
  twenty-two successful restitutions. Nine of those works have since been
  sold. (world.md)
- Article 19: a finding of fraud on an evidentiary document is grounds to
  reopen every restitution resting on that author's work. (world.md)
- Sebastiaan holds the only surviving original of the 1997 report, from the
  Maurice Faller estate archive bought in 2019. (world.md)
- The 1997 report also implicates Lucien Corvelijn, who is dead and beyond
  prosecution. (characters.md)
- Lena has €2,340. Vervoort's retainer is €6,000. (world.md, ch_07)
- Money in this world can buy a clerk's advance copy, a three-day delay on a
  date-stamp, a locksmith, a landlord, a valuation, or a building. (world.md)
- Money in this world cannot buy a Commission decision, a tribunal date, a
  reinstated archive accreditation, a closed criminal file, or Ruth
  Schindler-Wolff. (world.md)
- The firm's reach covers Antwerp, Brussels, the Belgian trade and one clerk.
  It does not reach the Academy, the Netherlands, Switzerland, or any
  magistrate. (world.md)

## Agreements & Limits

- Article 11 of the Commission's procedure: the docket is append-only.
  Nothing filed is ever removed. A corrigendum corrects; it does not erase.
  (world.md, ch_05)
- A corrigendum may be filed by any signatory to the original, at any time,
  without leave. Stated by Vervoort in ch_07 and by Rachida in ch_31.
  (ch_07, ch_31)
- Lena signs a confidentiality undertaking on 15 January without a lawyer.
  (ch_03)
- Lena's three terms, agreed aloud by Sebastiaan on 12 February: the 1997
  report produced that day; no door she cannot open from the inside; her
  registration number never to appear on anything again. (ch_13)
- Sebastiaan honours the first term with a laser print and keeps the
  original. (ch_14)
- The second term holds until 15 March. (ch_25)
- The third term is never breached in letter. (outline.md)
- The word that ends it, set by Lena on 26 February, is "Basel". (ch_19)
- On the third-floor landing on 26 February, both parties state plainly what
  the encounter was. (ch_19)
- Armand asks Lena on 12 February to stop protecting him. She refuses.
  (ch_13)
- On 8 May Armand agrees not to walk into Rue de la Loi, on condition that
  Lena stops treating him as a thing to be protected. (ch_34)
- Rachida gives Lena a verbal assurance on 15 May that she will not use
  Article 19 against Armand's work, and refuses to put it in writing.
  (ch_36)
- The Academy fellowship deadline is 1 June. The board meets once, on 2 May.
  (ch_01, ch_34)
- Kasimir Ott's four rules: nothing that leaves a mark a hospital would ask
  about; nothing on insured premises; nobody with a lawyer on retainer;
  seventy-two hours maximum. (ch_08)
- Kasimir breaks his own fourth rule by eight days in March. (ch_25)
- Sebastiaan never gives a verbal instruction on 14 March. He says nothing.
  (ch_24)

## Harm & Aftermath

- Lena's right scaphoid was broken at nineteen on the Kammenstraat cobbles
  and united badly. It aches below about eight degrees. (characters.md)
- Lena was held at the Deurne depot from 15 to 25 March, eleven days, in a
  building held between five and nine degrees. (ch_25)
- Lena was walked to the van by the upper arms on 15 March; the bruising was
  finger-shaped and took eleven days to yellow. (ch_25, ch_28)
- Lena reached the depot yard on day six, 20 March, via the freight lift's
  interlock, and was walked back. (ch_25)
- Lena moved terracotta pallets twice a day at the depot and wrote the Zurich
  argument in pencil on the back of a delivery manifest. (ch_25)
- By day nine Lena could not hold a pencil for more than four minutes.
  (ch_25)
- Lena did not see a doctor until 4 April, nine days after release; the
  contemporaneous record is lost. (ch_28)
- Diagnosis, 4 April: ulnar compression numbness, resolving in about three
  weeks; a fine tremor visible at three times magnification, permanent.
  (ch_28)
- Lena can no longer do invisible infill under a stereo microscope. She can
  still do lining, pressing, visible repair and teaching. (ch_28)
- **Nothing in this book restores Lena's steady hand.** (world.md,
  outline.md)
- Lena cannot sleep with a door shut, from 25 March onward. (ch_26)
- Lena puts her right hand flat on a table before doing anything fine, from
  April onward. It is never explained in the text. (characters.md)
- Tomas Beke was arrested on 6 February on a planted archive inventory card;
  charges were dropped in April; his accreditation was not restored, because
  accreditation is administrative and does not follow an acquittal. (ch_11,
  ch_36)
- Tomas Beke is selling secondhand books on Kloosterstraat, four doors from
  number 118, on 15 May. (ch_36)
- Tomas Beke's partner would not open the door past the chain on 6 February.
  (ch_11)
- Lena recommended Tomas Beke for the 2019 Academy loan whose dispute barred
  the firm from the premises. (ch_11)
- The Academy suspended Lena on 27 March and returned her 4B key on 19 May.
  (ch_27, ch_38)
- The Academy fellowship is lost and does not come back. (ch_34, ch_38)
- Lena's own disclosure of 5 May drew a reprimand on her record, not a
  suspension. (ch_34)
- Emiel Vandewiele had been under a cardiologist since November, mentioned in
  ch_08 and ch_16 before his death. (ch_08, ch_16)
- Emiel Vandewiele died on 8 May of a cardiac event in his own kitchen, aged
  74. No character caused it. (ch_33)
- Nobody is killed by another character in this book. Nobody in the trade
  owns a gun. (world.md)
- Kasimir Ott resigned on 14 May and was not punished by anyone. (ch_35)

## Character Facts

- Hélène "Lena" Brassart is thirty-three, a paper conservator, registration
  number B-4471, ten years on the register, divorced at twenty-nine.
  (characters.md, ch_01)
- Lena has a white scar across the base of her right thumb from a scalpel at
  twenty-two. (characters.md)
- Lena wears two thin layers year-round and cuts her hair short for suction
  table work. (characters.md)
- Lena can manufacture paper and iron-gall ink to laboratory standard,
  taught by Armand before she was twenty. Her CV and register entry show
  conservation only. (characters.md)
- Nobody living knows Lena can forge except Armand. Sebastiaan learns on 12
  April, from an auditor. (characters.md, ch_29)
- Lena saw her father rebinding a 1943 inventory book at twenty-three and
  said nothing. (characters.md)
- Lena saw Armand's second forgery in 2009 and has told nobody until 5 May.
  (characters.md, ch_32)
- Lena checks a hygrometer twice in four minutes when she is upset.
  (characters.md)
- Sebastiaan Corvelijn is forty-one, sole partner and *bewindvoerder* of
  Corvelijn & Zonen, nine years in the chair, divorced from Meike in 2018.
  (characters.md, ch_02)
- Sebastiaan has one permanent ink callus on the middle finger of his right
  hand and refuses to wear reading glasses in front of clients.
  (characters.md)
- Sebastiaan prints his name in block capitals on a scrap before signing
  anything. He does not do this on 5 May. (characters.md, ch_33)
- Sebastiaan becomes more accurate — dates, sums, page numbers — when he is
  lying. Lena identifies this on 28 February. (characters.md, ch_20)
- Sebastiaan does not sit down in his own house. (characters.md)
- Sebastiaan touches the doorframe of the white room and does not go in,
  from 24 January to 26 February. (characters.md, ch_19)
- Sebastiaan found the Pechstein in the Ghent sacristy. (ch_14)
- Sebastiaan knows that Lucien forged nine instruments across eleven years,
  and has known since 2016, and has told nobody. (characters.md, ch_31)
- Four current claims rest on Lucien's nine instruments. (ch_31, ch_37)
- Armand Brassart is seventy-one, retired, widowed since 1999. (characters.md)
- Armand wants to be prosecuted and says so twice. (characters.md, ch_13,
  ch_34)
- Emiel Vandewiele is seventy-four, chair of the Deurne Vier, and was in
  rope and cordage before finance. (characters.md)
- Emiel lent Lucien Corvelijn 900,000 francs on a handshake in 1991 and was
  repaid early. (ch_16)
- Hanne Vandewiele is forty-six, Emiel's daughter, an insolvency lawyer in
  Ghent, and uses statutory section numbers in conversation. (characters.md)
- Rachida Bekkali is forty-seven, senior registrar at the Commission,
  nineteen years in the registry. Her own family's claim was refused in 2004
  and she processed the refusal. (characters.md)
- Kasimir Ott is fifty-two, depot manager, twenty-one years with the firm,
  Lucien's man before Sebastiaan's, and never finishes a conditional
  sentence. (characters.md)
- Kasimir keeps a ledger of favours in a school exercise book going back to
  2003, and takes it with him when he resigns. (world.md, ch_35)
- Souad Ferhat is thirty-five, a third-generation bookbinder in
  Sint-Andries, and swears in three languages. (characters.md)
- Dries Neefs is thirty-eight, a reporter at *De Wacht*, and will not publish
  without date-stamps. (characters.md)
- Bram Six is sixty-one, a Commission clerk, mortgaged, and was Lucien's
  contact before Sebastiaan's. (characters.md, world.md)
- Ruth Schindler-Wolff is eighty-eight and lives in Basel. (characters.md)
- Meike Corvelijn is forty-four and entirely without rancour. (characters.md)
- Ineke Claes is sixty-three and cleans Kloosterstraat on Tuesdays and
  Fridays at 6 a.m. (characters.md)
- Griet Vervoort is fifty-five, an advocaat in Brussels, and gives two
  meetings on credit and then stops. (characters.md)

## Established In-Story (things that happened in chapters)

- Sebastiaan forged Lena's signature and registration number on a forty-page
  condition report and filed it on 18 January. This cannot be unfiled.
  (ch_04)
- Lena travelled to Brussels on 22 January and declined to answer Rachida's
  question about authorship. Rachida remembers. (ch_05)
- Lena refused to sign the Feininger report on 31 January and the refusal was
  never overridden. The claim stalled from 31 January to 5 May. (ch_09)
- Lena left an unsigned true condition report on the white-room table on 31
  January. It is still there on 31 March and she takes it with her on 14
  April. (ch_09, ch_27, ch_30)
- Sebastiaan said "do it" about Tomas Beke on 2 February. (ch_10)
- Lena burned a laser print on 12 February believing it was the original.
  (ch_13, ch_14)
- Lena discovered on 28 February that it was a copy, from the absence of a
  paperclip rust-mark. (ch_20)
- Lena manufactured a 1953 Basel loan receipt on 22 February and put it in
  the Zurich annex file. She did this alone and told no one. (ch_17)
- Lena and Sebastiaan set terms aloud on 26 February and confirmed
  afterwards what it had been. (ch_19)
- Sebastiaan lodged a summary of Armand's 1997 report on the preliminary
  docket on 4 March. Rachida pulled the entry. (ch_22)
- Lena gave Dries Neefs a partial document set on 11 March, withholding all
  1997 material. (ch_23)
- *De Wacht* published on 12 March. Clause 22 fired the same morning.
  (ch_23)
- Sebastiaan said nothing on 14 March when Kasimir proposed moving her, and
  went to Brussels for three days with his phone on silent. (ch_24)
- Sebastiaan learned on 18 March and came on 25 March. Lena worked this out
  from a timestamp in the van and said it aloud. He did not deny it. (ch_26)
- Sebastiaan tried to intervene at the Academy on 27 March and was turned
  away at the door under the 2019 standing minute. (ch_27)
- Sebastiaan did not sack Kasimir. Kasimir said, "You didn't say no, Bas."
  (ch_27)
- Lena said aloud on 4 April that she could no longer hold a scalpel steady.
  Sebastiaan did not answer. (ch_28)
- Sebastiaan named Lena as the forger of the 1953 receipt on 12 April, to
  Emiel Vandewiele and an auditor, with her registration number in the
  sentence. He had a stated alternative and did not take it. (ch_29)
- Emiel told Sebastiaan on 12 April: "Your father would have done that too."
  (ch_29)
- Lena left Kloosterstraat on 14 April using the alarm code 1109 and took
  only her own property. (ch_30)
- Sebastiaan opened the four cellar boxes on 18 April and found the 1997 file
  was one of nine. (ch_31)
- Rachida told Sebastiaan on 18 April: "You made her signature into a thing
  you could spend." (ch_31)
- Lena wrote out her account of 22 February in longhand on 24 April and
  decided to file it before anyone asked. (ch_32)
- Sebastiaan filed the corrigendum and the clause 9 resignation at 15:40 on
  5 May. Lena filed her own account the same afternoon. They did not speak.
  (ch_33)
- The referral against B-4471 was withdrawn on the evening of 5 May; a fresh
  referral was opened against Sebastiaan. (ch_33)
- The Commission struck Sebastiaan from the register for five years on 14
  May. He may not appear, file, or take a contingent commission in Belgium
  until he is forty-six. (ch_35)
- The claim book left Kloosterstraat 118 under Commission seal on 14 May.
  Sixty claims. (ch_35)
- The index — eleven drawers and a laptop — did not leave, and nobody from
  the Commission asked about it. (ch_35)
- The Corvelijn name came off the door on 14 May. The ghost of the lettering
  is still in the brick. (ch_35)
- Ruth Schindler-Wolff came to Antwerp on 15 May and was told the truth about
  the 1948 Basel restoration. She had already suspected. (ch_36)
- The Zurich tribunal ruled in the Faller matter on 19 May, awarding €6.2
  million to the Corvelijn escrow. The proceeding had run nine years and
  nobody in this book influenced its timetable. (ch_37)
- The Commission directed the first tranche of the Faller award to the
  twenty-two Brassart-authenticated restitutions and the four claims resting
  on Lucien's instruments. Sebastiaan does not administer the fund. (ch_37)
- Hanne Vandewiele wrote off the €4.1 million against the escrowed claim book
  at a probate valuation on 19 May, and said twice that it was not a
  gesture. (ch_37)
- The Schindler-Wolff estate declined to press the criminal referral. Without
  a complainant with standing, the *parket* filed it. (ch_37)
- Sebastiaan accepted provenance research work from a Ghent museum on 19 May;
  research is outside the scope of the five-year bar. (ch_37)
- Lena's 4B key was returned on 19 May. The fellowship was already gone.
  (ch_38)
- On 21 May Lena chose to stay, and said the reason was not what he gave up.
  (ch_38)

## Noted discrepancies for the next pass

- ch_25 gives the depot's temperature range as five to nine degrees;
  world.md gives the same range but ties the wrist ache to "below about
  eight degrees". Both can be true, but drafting should not state a single
  fixed depot temperature.
- world.md says the firm's staff is six; the outline names only Sebastiaan,
  Kasimir and Ineke plus an unnamed junior in ch_02. The remaining two need
  names before drafting, or the staff count should come down to four.
